cards.headline: She'd never heard of Gorillaz — and was surprised Albarn still made music
cards.snippet: Yukimi Nagano had never heard of Gorillaz when the collaboration was proposed, and was ambivalent about it; when her manager explained that Damon Albarn was the singer from Blur, she was mildly surprised he still made music. “I definitely wasn't as charged as I perhaps might have been if I knew who they were,” she later said. “Everyone was telling me it was a big deal.” At Albarn's Studio 13 in London, he played her instrumental tracks and let her choose; the ones she picked became “Empire Ants” and “To Binge,” recorded over several days, with all four members of Little Dragon credited as writers alongside Albarn.
cards.context: Albarn had been introduced to Little Dragon by his partner Suzi Winstanley, who was a fan of the band.

cards.headline: Two songs in one: a ballad that hands over to a machine groove
cards.snippet: “Empire Ants” runs 4:43 in two distinct halves. The first is a drifting, synth-washed Albarn ballad — BBC Music called it “a trickling ballad to rank alongside Blur's best.” Around the halfway mark, rising arpeggios flip the track into an electro-funk groove and Nagano takes the lead, singing of little feet working the machine and empires falling like waves. Pitchfork called Little Dragon's contributions to Plastic Beach “airy, elusive, and amazingly beautiful”; ZME Music went further, calling this “the best song on the album by a wide margin” — an album cut, never a single, carried by word of mouth.
cards.context: Nagano's voice appears twice on Plastic Beach: “Empire Ants” (track 7) and “To Binge” (track 14).

cards.headline: The pool's most-liked comment marvels at the band's very existence
cards.snippet: It's just mind blowing, about how a cartoonist and a guitar player meet up one day and say, let's create an imaginary band with all these different people. It's amazing about how this band came to life, and became real. It's something else. I'm just... blown away
cards.context: Gorillaz are the creation of Damon Albarn and artist Jamie Hewlett — a musician and a cartoonist, as the comment says.

replies.author: @ididntsaybanana
replies.text: I totally feel you. I dread the possibility that what if they never met:(

cards.headline: “Murdoc wrote this” — the in-joke that lays fans flat
cards.snippet: sometimes i think about the fact that murdoc wrote this and i have to just lay down
cards.context: In Gorillaz canon, Murdoc Niccals is the band's fictional founder; the songs are Albarn's, but fans credit Murdoc in-universe.

replies.author: @charonsferryreal
replies.text: And that Noodle wrote Demon Days.

replies.author: @kottonkandy0962
replies.text: He's so sad and tormented, no wonder he writes stuff like this.

cards.headline: Six thousand likes for a single image: a sunset over the oceans
cards.snippet: this song sounds like a sunset over the oceans
cards.context: A seascape is this song's home terrain: sailing out of the doldrums, empires falling like waves, on an album called Plastic Beach.

replies.author: @gootrooper8585
replies.text: When the sun sets, the strobe lights come out to play.

replies.author: @smoking_poetry
replies.text: All in all, its purple/yellowish sunset over the ocean and there is only one person in the entire beach enjoying the view while rain drops descend from the sky and slowly slide through your face. But you're not on earth all this is taking place in another planet.

cards.headline: How nice the world can be, yet how terrible it is
cards.snippet: This song gives me the feels about how nice the world can be yet how terrible it is
cards.context: That duality is the song in miniature — a lullaby that watches the world end, then a dance groove over the fall of empires.

replies.author: @ohmy6534
replies.text: melancholy is the word you're looking for

replies.author: @StarlightTheCat_lol
replies.text: Agreed, it's very unnerving. One time when I was 15 I ran away from home and it was almost 4 am and I listened to this while walking in the dark and it was so surreal. Now my life is doing way better and I'm pleased for the future.

cards.headline: Live on Letterman, 2010: the full band, every sound played live
cards.snippet: Gorillaz performed the song on the Late Show with David Letterman in October 2010, during the Escape to Plastic Beach tour, with Nagano singing her half while a full live band recreated the studio arrangement. One listener: “Do you think those audience members realize how lucky they are?”
cards.context: Posted to the band's own channel, it remains the song's most-watched live performance by an order of magnitude.

version.versionLabel: Gorillaz - Empire Ants feat. Little Dragon (Live on Letterman)

cards.headline: Outside Lands 2017: the reunion, seven years on
cards.snippet: At Outside Lands in San Francisco on 11 August 2017, Nagano joined Gorillaz for the song's first performance since 2010. Albarn told the crowd they hadn't played it because “we haven't really seen Yukimi since then.”
cards.context: She had toured the song with the band throughout 2010, including the Coachella set she later called a turning point for her as an artist.

version.versionLabel: Gorillaz - Empire Ants (feat. Yukimi Nagano of Little Dragon) – Outside Lands 2017
